extraction_warnings: Supplemental Table S1 likely contains per-subject demographic and exposure data (age, sex, travel destination, diarrhea, antimalarial use) not included in the provided text; sample-level granularity could not be extracted.
Sex and subcohort fields reflect cohort-level proportions/counts rather than single categorical values, as the cohort is mixed across destinations and sexes.
ENA accession (PRJEB7369) provided under 'ncbi_accession' field though it is technically a European Nucleotide Archive accession, not NCBI.
No explicit disease/health status statement found; participants appear to be healthy travelers but this was not directly stated.

This paper is about travel-associated gut microbiome/antibiotic resistance gene changes, not disease/oncology/neonatal/FMT contexts; most schema fields designed for clinical/oncology studies are not applicable and were marked not_reported.

feces_phenotype, feces_phenotype_value, biomarker_name/value/unit, and treatment fields were populated using best-fit interpretation of schema intent (stool-related phenotypes and resistance gene abundance measurements); confidence set to medium due to interpretive mapping.
No explicit 'Healthy' disease status statement was found for disease_details despite study subjects appearing to be non-diseased travelers; field marked not_reported to avoid fabrication.
study_name field could not be determined from the provided text; no canonical study identifier format (e.g., 'AuthorX_YYYY') appears in the paper.
dna_extraction_kit not explicitly named in the main text; details likely reside in supplemental material not provided.
Two sequencing platforms are mentioned (Illumina HiSeq 2000 for metagenomics, Illumina MiSeq for isolate genomes); only the primary metagenomic platform was extracted per schema intent.

target_condition is not a single disease label; the study investigates antibiotic resistance gene acquisition and ESBL colonization associated with international travel, which does not map cleanly to a single NCIT/EFO condition term.
